one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 results are expected in early December 2026, after 2026-10-30. The events that already happened are the CEO's exit to Meta on about 2026-09-25/26 (-18% to -22% in a day, and about -25% over the month from $446.62) and the 2026-09-29 Investor Day (targets raised, extra $1B buyback), which lifted the stock from about $328-335 to $356. Possible events inside the window: news on a permanent CEO (unscheduled; naming someone credible would help, a long search is neutral to slightly negative), the new buyback being put to work (a small support), and macro/software-sector moves. I see no reliable edge in which way a post-shock rebound goes next, so I use a roughly symmetric lognormal centred on $357 with a monthly sigma of about 16.5%. That is a little below the 71%/3.5 rule of thumb, because the realized vol is inflated by two event gaps that are now in the past.

fair_value.method: A blend of the NTM P/E ($9.9 NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 x 36x = $356), EV/NTM sales ($4.2B x 7.0x + ~$3.0B net cash over 85.8M fully diluted shares = $378) and an FCF-yield check ($0.94B FY29 FCF at a 3.3% yield + $3.0B net cash = $367). The multiples are set below growth-software peers because stock comp is about 20% of revenue and the $1.91/share Q2 SBC add-back exceeds the whole $1.90 non-GAAP EPS.

inputs_detail.derivation: The low end of management's new 3-year '>20%' target (Investor Day), which the skeptic case takes because the Q3 guide already implies only 20-21% and Atlas growth has sat at 29% for three quarters.
The midpoint of the 100-200bp/yr target, applied to the FY27 guided margin.
FY29 revenue ~$4.35B x 23.8% = ~$1.04B op income + ~$80M interest, taxed at ~21%, over ~85M FD shares = ~$10.4 FY29; blended with Q4 FY28 = ~$9.9.

Below growth-software peers (~40-45x for ~20% growers) because SBC is ~20% of revenue ($148.9M in Q2 on $771.8M) and non-GAAP EPS is almost all SBC add-back; the extra risk of a CEO search also argues for a discount.

methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Sep-2027 $4.2B x 7.0x = $29.4B EV + ~$3.0B net cash, / 85.8M FD shares

inputs_detail.derivation: The FY27 midpoint of $3.01B grown 20%/yr gives FY28 $3.61B and FY29 $4.34B; the NTM window at Sep-2027 is mostly FY29, so ~$4.2B.
Today's EV is ~$26.8B ($356 x ~82M shares less $2.4B cash) on ~$3.5B NTM sales = ~7.6x. I take a modest de-rate as growth settles toward 20% and Postgres/hyperscaler competition persists.

inputs_detail.value: $2.4B, no convertible debt outstanding on the balance sheet

inputs_detail.derivation: $2.4B plus ~$0.75B of NTM FCF, less part of the new $1B buyback used to offset SBC dilution.
The midpoint of the Investor Day target; management says it implies >$1B FCF in FY30.
Unadjusted FCF is inflated by ~$600M/yr of SBC (Q2 SBC $148.9M). A 3.3% headline yield equals roughly a 1% SBC-adjusted yield, which I treat as the most a skeptic should pay for a ~20% grower.

bear.story: Atlas slips from 29% to the low 20s as frontier-lab/AI-native spend (only 3-5% of Atlas) fails to offset Postgres/pgvector and hyperscaler competition. The CEO search drags on or lands on a weak candidate, and consumption softens in Q4. The market re-rates to ~5x NTM sales / ~25x EPS and focuses on GAAP EPS of under $1. This is similar to the March 2026 reset to ~$216-260, when Baird, KeyBanc and Wells downgraded.

base.story: Revenue grows ~20-22% with 150bp/yr of margin expansion, a credible permanent CEO is named by mid-2027, and the $1B buyback offsets dilution. The stock recovers part of the leadership discount but stays below the pre-exit $446 while the SBC-quality debate caps the multiple at ~36x NTM EPS.

bull.story: RPO (+91%) and cRPO (+73%) turn into faster growth, Atlas re-accelerates above 30% on AI workloads, and the 'Rule of 50' path gains credibility. The stock rerates to ~9x sales, toward the sell-side average of ~$457 and the high of $565.

thesis_break_reason: At about $240 (-33%) the stock would be back near the March-2026 post-guide low (52-week low $215.68). Getting there without a market crash most likely means a real fundamental break: Atlas growth falling toward 20% or lower, a guide-down in Dec-2026 or Mar-2027, or more senior departures during the CEO search. That is more than leadership noise, and it would invalidate the investor-day >20% growth framework.

catalysts.event: Permanent CEO search updates / possible naming of successor
Q3 FY27 results (guide $756-761M, 20-21% growth); watch Atlas growth vs the stagnant 29%
Q4 FY27 results and first FY28 guide; the March-2026 guide caused a -22% day
Q1 FY28 results; MongoDB.local events / AI product updates

key_uncertainties: Whether the permanent CEO is credible and how long the search takes; this is the second CEO change in under 12 months
Whether Atlas growth, stuck at ~29% for three quarters, holds or decelerates as the Q3 guide implies overall growth of ~20-21%
Earnings quality: SBC of ~$600M/yr versus non-GAAP EPS; FY27 GAAP EPS is guided at only $0.53-0.77
Competition from Postgres (serverless Postgres, pgvector) and hyperscalers (Microsoft Postgres revenue +55%) on new AI workloads
How much the unusually high RPO/cRPO growth depends on large multi-year EA deals that inflate reported growth now and set up tough comps later
reasoning: Facts: Q2 FY27 revenue was $771.8M (+30%), Atlas +29%, a 24% non-GAAP operating margin, FCF of $137.6M, $2.4B of cash and no convertible debt outstanding. FY27 guidance was raised to $2.99-3.03B with non-GAAP EPS of $6.39-6.58 but GAAP EPS of only $0.53-0.77. The bear evidence I found: (1) the stock fell 13.6% after a beat-and-raise because Atlas growth has been flat at 29% for three quarters and the Q3 guide implies ~20-21% growth; (2) SBC of ~$153M in the quarter is 94% of non-GAAP net income, and the SBC add-back per share exceeds non-GAAP EPS; (3) the CEO left for Meta after 11 months, the day before Investor Day, making it the second CEO change in a year, and the stock fell ~25% over the month from $446.62 to ~$328-335; (4) Postgres and hyperscaler competition is intensifying (Microsoft Postgres +55%), and AI-native customers are only 3-5% of Atlas; (5) the March-2026 guide reset caused a -22% day and a string of downgrades (Baird, KeyBanc, Wells), showing how sensitive this name is to guidance. Weighing it honestly: the business is not broken. Guidance was reaffirmed after the CEO exit, Investor Day raised the 3-year targets (>20% growth, 100-200bp/yr of margin expansion, 80-100% FCF conversion, >$1B FCF in FY30) and added a $1B buyback, the balance sheet is clean, and insider selling is small (a director's 10b5-1 sale of 1,000 shares at $375.92). Most sell-side targets are $460-565 (average ~$457), which the skeptic lane discounts because targets lagged the March reset. My fair value is ~$368 (P/E 36x on $9.9 NTM EPS, 7x EV/sales, and an FCF-yield check), only slightly above spot. Scenario mean ~$375 (bear $220 / base $380 / bull $530 at 25/50/25). For the ladder I used a lognormal with a median of ~$362 and sigma of ~0.52, slightly below the 71% realized vol because two past event gaps inflate that figure, while keeping the fat tails that the stock's history (a 52-week range of $216-$473) supports. Research was limited: SEC.gov rate-limited the Investor Day 8-K fetch, so the targets come from press summaries, and X/Twitter was not searched.
